title: Unit – 5 : Session – 6 : SLO – 1  |  Minimum Spanning Tree — Prim's Algorithm
sections: I. Graph Reference
II. Fill in the Blanks
The number of edges in a Minimum Spanning Tree for a graph with 6 vertices is 5.
The first edge selected by Prim's algorithm starting from vertex 1 is 1-4 (weight 1).
The edge with the next minimum weight connected to the MST is 1-2 (weight 2).
The total weight of the MST obtained is 17.
Prim's algorithm uses a VISITED SET (visited array / min-priority queue) to track the vertices already included in the MST.
III. True or False
Prim's algorithm selects the highest weight edge available at each step — FALSE (minimum weight).
The MST constructed for this graph will have 5 edges — TRUE (n-1 = 5).
Prim's algorithm forms cycles while adding edges — FALSE (it only adds edges to unvisited vertices).
The edge 3-6 (8) will be included in the MST if lower weight connections are available — FALSE
(edge 2-6 with weight 7 is lower, so 3-6 is excluded).
IV. Short Answer Questions
Prim's algorithm grows the MST from a starting vertex; at each step it picks the MINIMUM-WEIGHT edge that
connects a vertex already in the MST to a vertex outside it.
Prim's MST algorithm assumes an UNDIRECTED, connected, weighted graph; in directed graphs the notion of a
spanning tree differs (arborescence), and negative weights break the greedy 'minimum edge' justification.
A MIN-PRIORITY QUEUE (binary heap) makes Prim's algorithm more efficient than a simple array: O(E log V).
V. Apply Prim's Algorithm Starting from Vertex 1
Step 1: MST = {1}. Min edge out: 1-4 (1). Select 1-4.
Order of edges selected: 1-4, 1-2, 2-3, 1-5, 2-6.
TOTAL WEIGHT OF MST = 1 + 2 + 3 + 4 + 7 = 17.
